channel.title: Vigil — Notes
channel.description: Field guides to geometric and rounded sans serifs, the typefaces hiding in public life, and notes from the making of Vigil.

item.title: License plate fonts: shaped by a die, aimed at a forger
item.description: There is no single license plate font. The letterforms were shaped by a stamping die, hardened against tape-and-paint forgery, and are now drawn for cameras.
item.dc:creator: Keno Vigil

item.title: Highway Gothic vs Clearview: two fonts went to war over American road signs
item.description: American road signs use Highway Gothic, drawn in 1948. A rival called Clearview was approved in 2004, killed in 2016 and revived in 2018.
item.dc:creator: Keno Vigil

item.title: Geometric sans serif fonts: a field guide
item.description: What makes a sans serif geometric, how to spot one in four seconds, and which geometric sans serif fonts are actually worth using.
item.dc:creator: Keno Vigil

item.title: Typeface vs font: the distinction that stopped mattering in 1985
item.description: A typeface is the design; a font was one size and one style of it, cast in metal. Where the distinction came from, and why digital type dissolved it.
item.dc:creator: Keno Vigil

item.title: A vigil is what you keep when you refuse to go to sleep on something.
item.description: Ten years of a calendar block that said MAKE FONT, and why it finally shipped.
item.dc:creator: Keno Vigil

item.title: A century of circles: the geometric grotesk
item.description: Erbar, Futura and Kabel arrived within a year of each other in 1926-27 and defined a category still with us.
item.dc:creator: Keno Vigil

item.title: Soft corners: a short history of the rounded sans
item.description: Helvetica Rounded, VAG Rounded and the app-icon era, and the uniform-rounding mistake most of them make.
item.dc:creator: Keno Vigil
